findings.description: steerSession now throws TerminalSessionError, and the watchdog's catch (turn-watchdog.service.ts L125-130) still filters on isRefusedSteer only, so a session that is killed or merged mid-sweep aborts the rest of that sweep instead of being skipped.

If launchWatcher throws after the conductor's kickoff landed, startConductor throws with the conductor window still running. `pup conductor start` then crashes without printing the started/attach lines it printed before the move, and the TUI reports a failure for a conductor that is up.
The `LaunchRolledBackError` JSDoc says `launchTask` and `startConductor` are "the only two functions that open a window on a compiled context", but `respawnSession` also does.

The PR promotes the CLI's private `isRefusedSteer` to an exported core helper, but leaves the identical private copy in `src/core/turn-watchdog.service.ts:237-239`, so core now has two definitions of the same refusal predicate (decisions 45/46) that can drift apart; the watchdog should import the new export.

`rolledBackLine` rebuilds the exact text that the `LaunchRolledBackError` constructor already puts in `error.message`. The format is now defined in two places, and a change to one will quietly diverge from the other.

The new `rolledBackLaunch` helper was inserted between `seedKilledSession` and its JSDoc. The old comment now sits on its own, stacked on top of the new helper's JSDoc, and `seedKilledSession` has lost its doc.
the comment is a history narration ("as it always has", "which is why the CLI printed it before killing back when the rollback lived there").
"Nothing landed yet, so nothing is on record if this refuses." narrates the control flow rather than a hidden invariant.
the inline comment ("A window with no context is a bypass-permissions agent… killed, not left to inspect") restates what `rollBackRefusedLaunch`'s JSDoc and the `startConductor` JSDoc already say.
the new JSDoc blocks are very long: `deliverKickoff`, `startRadarWith`, `steerSession`, `LaunchRolledBackError` and `requireLiveSession` each run 8-14 lines of prose.

When the conductor or a session runs `pup interrupt <s> <message>`, the steer is still recorded as `{kind:'interrupt'}` with no `by`. This is the same misattribution that commit d96d1ea fixed for `pup steer`'s typed path: the sender is worked out there but never passed to `interruptSession`.

To find the latest handoff request, `signalledHash` searches the whole steer payload for the text `handoff-request`. A session controls the `by` field (through `PUP_SESSION_ID`, after `cd`-ing out of its worktree), so it can plant that text and fake a request. Decision 44 says an unrequested `handoff_ready` should make no session ready, and this breaks that.

process_issues.description: review-context was not spawned because no spec, protocol or infra surface is touched. review-security ran as a single instance although the diff passes the size gate, since the only trust-boundary surface is the steer/rollback shell-outs.
The conventions reviewer said it did not read testing.md, the test files, the src/cli/index.ts diff or docs/09-decisions.md, so convention coverage of those files is partial.

The docs reviewer's important finding (LaunchRolledBackError JSDoc 'only two functions') was CONFIRMED by the validator, which recommended a nit: the sentence describes who throws the error and no caller relies on it. The orchestrator downgraded it to nit.
